why-the-next-industrial-race-will-be-won.title_en: Why the next industrial race will be won on electricity
why-the-next-industrial-race-will-be-won.title_zh: 为何下一场工业竞赛的胜负取决于电力
paras_en: September 15 - For two centuries, industry has followed energy. Factories gathered around coalfields, refineries around ports and pipelines, energy-hungry industries went where fuel was plentiful and cheap. Google recently announced a 13 billion euros investment in digital and AI infrastructure in Finland, its largest single investment in Europe, alongside a 22-year nuclear power deal. The technology is new, but the industrial logic is old: reliable power attracts capital.

AI has made the return of electricity at the centre of economic policy impossible to miss. But data centres are part of a much wider surge. The International Energy Agency expects global electricity consumption to grow at least 2.5 times faster than overall energy demand through to 2030, propelled by industry, electric vehicles, cooling, data centres and other new uses. After decades of sluggish electricity growth in many advanced economies, power demand is rising again.

Ember’s new Age of Power report argues that the digital revolution and electrification of the physical economy are beginning to converge. Chips, batteries, power electronics, motors and sensors now underpin technologies ranging from AI servers to electric cars and grid batteries – expansion in one market can drive down costs and improve capability in others. Economies that can combine digital capability with cheap, scalable electricity and rapid electrification, Ember argues, will be better-placed to attract investment and build the industries that grow around them.

That will reshape the geography of economic power. Coal, oil and gas gave some countries an advantage by geological accident and left much of the world dependent on fuel shipped across oceans or through pipelines.

Sun and wind are spread far more widely: Ember calculates that 97% of people live in countries with renewable resources capable of producing more than 10 times their current electricity demand. Turning that physical potential into economic advantage depends on things countries can actually build and improve, such as generation, grids, storage, skills, markets and institutions.

In China , electricity already supplies 28% of its final energy consumption, compared with 22% in the United States and 21% in the European Union. Chinese industry is also becoming more electricity-intensive. The factories producing solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles consumed more than 300 terrawatt hours (TWh) in 2024 – about as much electricity as Italy uses in a year. It is also pursuing electrification and automation together, a combination that Ember argues can accelerate growth in both.

Europe has large renewable resources and some of the world’s most ambitious climate policy, but expensive power continues to bear down on industry. The European Central Bank estimates that electricity prices for energy-intensive industries rose by around 53% between 2019 and 2024. Their electricity consumption fell by about 14.5% between 2019 and 2023.
A continent trying simultaneously to decarbonise, re-industrialise and compete in new technologies cannot risk high electricity prices becoming a competitive disadvantage.

Business leaders already see electrification through this competitive lens. Recent global polling of business executives found 90% expect their operations to be largely electrified by 2035, 88% believe electrification will make their businesses more competitive and 91% expect it to deliver greater energy security.
Yet 72% say government policy is moving too slowly, and 62% would consider moving operations to another country if they could not get enough support to electrify.

The pace of electrification will be front and centre at Climate Week NYC. Energy and electrification are set to run through the week’s business and political agenda, while the incoming COP31 presidency in Turkey has already made electrification one of its headline priorities, setting a goal for electricity to supply 35% of global final energy demand by 2035.

Two obstacles to rapid progress stand out. The first is grids, with more than 2,500 gigawatts (GW ) of renewable generation, storage and large electricity loads currently sitting in connection queues worldwide. Major grid infrastructure can take five to 15 years to build.

The second is finance: in emerging and developing economies, the cost of capital for renewable power and batteries can be at least twice that in advanced economies. Cheap renewable resources are little advantage if businesses cannot connect to the power they produce.

For that reason, the next stage asks more of governments than adding gigawatts to renewable-energy targets. Power has to be affordable. New factories and equipment have to connect quickly. Networks have to use digital technology and flexible demand to get more from the wires already in the ground. Capital has to be cheap enough for countries with enormous renewable potential to turn it into productive electricity.

The economic map drawn by coal, oil and gas has lasted for generations; now electricity is beginning to redraw it. Natural resources will still matter, but institutions, infrastructure and investment will matter more. Countries that can make clean electricity cheaply, and move it where it is needed, will create an advantage that compounds as more of the economy goes electric.

paras_zh: 9月15日——两个世纪以来，工业一直追随着能源。工厂聚集在煤田周围，炼油厂建在港口和管道附近，能源密集型产业则迁往燃料充足且廉价的地方。谷歌最近宣布在芬兰投资130亿欧元建设数字和人工智能基础设施，这是其在欧洲的最大单笔投资，同时还签署了一项为期22年的核电协议。技术是新的，但产业逻辑是旧的：可靠的电力吸引资本。
人工智能使电力重新回到经济政策的核心位置，这一点已无法忽视。但数据中心只是更大浪潮的一部分。国际能源署（IEA）预计，到2030年，全球电力消费增速将至少是整体能源需求的2.5倍，推动因素包括工业、电动汽车、制冷、数据中心及其他新用途。在许多发达经济体经历了数十年的电力增长低迷之后，电力需求正在再次上升。
Ember最新发布的《电力时代》报告认为，数字革命与实体经济的电气化正开始交汇融合。芯片、电池、电力电子、电机和传感器如今支撑着从人工智能服务器到电动汽车和电网电池等各种技术——一个市场的扩张可以推动其他市场的成本下降和能力提升。Ember认为，那些能够将数字能力与廉价、可扩展的电力以及快速电气化相结合的经济体，将更有条件吸引投资并围绕这些产业建立配套产业。
这将重塑经济实力的地理格局。煤炭、石油和天然气因地质偶然性赋予了一些国家优势，却使世界大部分地区依赖于跨洋航运或管道输送的燃料。
太阳和风能的分布则广泛得多：Ember计算得出，97%的人口所在国家拥有的可再生资源，足以生产超过其当前电力需求10倍以上的电力。要将这种物理潜力转化为经济优势，取决于各国能否切实建设和改善发电、电网、储能、技能、市场和制度等要素。
在中国，电力已占最终能源消费的28%，而美国和欧盟分别为22%和21%。中国工业也正变得更加电力密集型。2024年，生产太阳能电池板、电池和电动汽车的工厂消耗了超过300太瓦时（TWh）的电力——大致相当于意大利一年的用电量。中国还在同时推进电气化和自动化，Ember认为这一组合能够加速两者的增长。
欧洲拥有丰富的可再生资源和全球最雄心勃勃的一些气候政策，但高昂的电价持续对工业形成压制。欧洲央行估计，2019年至2024年间，能源密集型行业的电价上涨了约53%。2019年至2023年间，这些行业的用电量下降了约14.5%。
一个同时试图脱碳、再工业化和在新兴技术领域竞争的大陆，不能让高电价成为竞争劣势。
商界领袖早已从竞争力的角度看待电气化。近期一项针对企业高管的全球调查发现，90%的受访者预计到2035年其运营将基本实现电气化，88%认为电气化将提升企业竞争力，91%预计电气化将带来更高的能源安全。
然而，72%的受访者表示政府政策推进过于缓慢，62%表示如果无法获得足够的电气化支持，他们会考虑将业务迁往其他国家。
电气化的步伐将成为纽约气候周的核心议题。能源与电气化预计将贯穿整个气候周的商业和政治议程，而即将上任的《联合国气候变化框架公约》第31次缔约方大会（COP31）主席国土耳其已将电气化列为头号优先事项之一，设定目标为到2035年电力占全球终端能源需求的35%。
快速推进面临两大突出障碍。其一是电网，目前全球有超过2500吉瓦（GW）的可再生能源发电、储能及大型用电负荷正在排队等待并网。大型电网基础设施的建设周期可长达五至十五年。
其次是融资问题：在新兴和发展中经济体，可再生能源发电和电池的资本成本至少是发达经济体的两倍。如果企业无法接入可再生能源所发的电力，那么廉价的可再生资源就没什么优势可言。
因此，下一阶段对政府的要求不仅仅是提高可再生能源目标的吉瓦数。电力必须价格可负担。新建工厂和设备必须能快速并网。电网必须利用数字技术和灵活的需求，从已有的线路中获取更多电力。对于可再生能源潜力巨大的国家来说，资本成本必须足够低，才能将其转化为有生产力的电力。
煤炭、石油和天然气所绘就的经济版图已经延续了几代人；如今，电力正开始重新绘制这一版图。自然资源仍将重要，但制度、基础设施和投资将更为关键。那些能够以低成本生产清洁电力并将其输送到所需之地的国家，将创造出一种随着经济日益电气化而不断累积的优势。

meta-s-zuckerberg-says-ai-labs-have-enou.title_en: Meta's Zuckerberg says AI labs have enough incentive to build safely
meta-s-zuckerberg-says-ai-labs-have-enou.title_zh: Meta的扎克伯格称AI实验室有足够动力安全构建
paras_en: - Summary
- Companies
- Zuckerberg says liability and competition give labs enough incentive to build AI safely
- Zuckerberg says Meta delayed Muse AI agent release earlier this year to strengthen security
- Meta directs significant majority of compute to user needs rather than AI self-improvement, Zuckerberg says

Sept 15 (Reuters) - Meta ​Platforms (META.O), opens new tab CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on Tuesday that competition and liability give AI companies enough reason to act individually ‌on safety, appearing to break from calls by leaders of top AI firms for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

The comments underscore a split among industry executives and U.S. authorities over how to respond to warnings that the technology is advancing faster than companies can control it, with some industry insiders warning ​it poses an existential threat to humanity .
The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

Zuckerberg, in an X post on Tuesday, said that every lab has the responsibility ​and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to ⁠take its own actions to ensure that happens.

His remarks come three days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged AI companies to slow ​the pace at which they improve model capabilities, on the heels of existential risk warnings by several researchers.
Rival OpenAI's chief Sam Altman and xAI's ​Elon Musk both publicly endorsed Amodei's call within hours.

President Donald Trump on Monday, however, downplayed concerns about AI's potential for harm, saying the U.S. already had guardrails in place for the technology and that China would benefit from doubt being cast on AI's development. The view that regulations will ​harm U.S. companies' ability to compete with their Chinese counterparts is shared by tech executives, including Nvidia (NVDA.O), opens new tab CEO Jensen Huang .

"Trust and alignment are ​quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models," Zuckerberg said Tuesday. "Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind."

Item 1 of 2 Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg delivers a speech, as the letters AI for artificial intelligence appear on screen, at the Meta Connect event at the company's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, U.S., September 27, 2023. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo

1/2] Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg delivers a speech, as the letters AI for artificial intelligence appear on screen, at the Meta Connect event at the company's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, U.S., September 27, 2023. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

Zuckerberg also ‌said Tuesday ⁠that labs had a strong incentive to prevent their models from causing harm as they would face "significant" liability otherwise. He pointed to Meta delaying the release of its Muse AI agent earlier this year to strengthen its security.
"We didn't call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and ​for us," he said.

While Amodei called for ⁠an industry-wide slowing of recursive self-improvement — AI's ability to improve itself — Zuckerberg said Meta had already committed the "significant majority" of its compute toward creating products that serve users' immediate needs rather than pursuing self-improving ​AI systems.

Zuckerberg also said Meta Superintelligence Labs — its AI division — already engaged independent evaluators in several ​areas, calling it "industry best ⁠practice" and that "other labs can just do this too".

Zuckerberg's push to position Meta as a responsible actor on AI safety comes weeks after the company agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle U.S. state lawsuits alleging it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict children, without admitting wrongdoing.

Adding ⁠to the ​uncertainty around any coordinated approach by AI firms, FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said Tuesday ​everyone should be " deeply suspicious " of AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions while lobbying for new regulations.
While Ferguson did not name Anthropic, Amodei last week requested antitrust permission to enable ​rivals to coordinate a slower pace to AI development due to safety concerns.
Reporting by Chris Thomas in Mexico City; Editing by Stephen Coates

paras_zh: 扎克伯格表示，责任与竞争已为实验室提供足够动力来安全地开发人工智能。
扎克伯格表示，Meta今年早些时候推迟了Muse AI代理的发布，以加强安全性。
Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格表示，公司将绝大多数算力用于满足用户需求，而非AI自我改进。
9月15日（路透社）——Meta Platforms（META.O）首席执行官马克·扎克伯格周二表示，竞争和法律责任足以让AI公司有理由各自采取安全行动，这似乎与顶尖AI企业领导人呼吁协调放缓AI开发的立场出现分歧。
这些言论凸显出行业高管与美国当局之间在如何回应相关警告上存在分歧——有警告称，该技术的推进速度已超过企业能够控制的程度，一些业内人士则警告称，这对人类构成生存威胁。
路透社每日简报通讯提供你开启一天所需的所有新闻。在此注册。
扎克伯格周二在X平台上发帖称，每个实验室都有责任和动力，按照安全训练模型所需的速度推进，并且有能力自行采取行动来确保这一点实现。
他的这番言论发表三天前，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊呼吁人工智能公司放缓提升模型能力的步伐，此前几位研究人员发出了生存风险警告。
竞争对手OpenAI的首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼和xAI的埃隆·马斯克都在数小时内公开支持了阿莫代伊的呼吁。
然而，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一淡化了人们对人工智能潜在危害的担忧，称美国已经为这项技术设置了护栏，而中国将从对人工智能发展的质疑中受益。包括英伟达（NVDA.O）首席执行官黄仁勋在内的科技高管们也认同这一观点，即监管将损害美国公司与中国同行竞争的能力。
“信任与对齐正迅速成为区分智能体与模型的最重要能力，”扎克伯格周二表示。“任何不专注于对齐的实验室都将落后。”
Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格发表演讲，屏幕上出现代表人工智能的AI字样，地点位于美国加利福尼亚州门洛帕克的公司总部，2023年9月27日。路透社/卡洛斯·巴里亚/资料照片
扎克伯格周二还表示，各实验室有强烈动机防止其模型造成伤害，否则将面临“重大”责任。他指出，Meta今年早些时候推迟了其Muse AI智能体的发布，以加强其安全性。
他说：“我们没有要求其他所有人先这样做，然后自己才做。我们只是把它作为日常工作的一部分，因为这对人们、对我们来说显然都是正确的事。”
虽然阿莫代伊呼吁全行业放缓递归自我改进——即人工智能自我提升的能力——但扎克伯格表示，Meta已经将其计算资源的“绝大多数”投入到创造服务用户即时需求的产品上，而不是追求自我改进的人工智能系统。
扎克伯格还表示，Meta超级智能实验室——其人工智能部门——已经在多个领域引入了独立评估机构，称这是“行业最佳实践”，并且“其他实验室也可以这样做”。
扎克伯格推动将Meta定位为人工智能安全方面的负责任参与者，此举距离该公司同意支付高达180亿美元以了结美国各州诉讼仅数周。这些诉讼指控Meta将Facebook和Instagram设计成让儿童上瘾，而Meta并未承认存在不当行为。
在人工智能公司任何协调行动的不确定性之上，美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）主席安德鲁·弗格森周二表示，对于寻求反垄断豁免同时又游说新监管的AI公司，所有人都应“深表怀疑”。
弗格森没有点名Anthropic，但阿莫代伊上周以安全担忧为由，请求反垄断许可，以便让竞争对手协调放慢AI开发步伐。
